outcome: The answer does not tell legal the deletion flow meets the policy, because etl_users appends users, including email and full_name, to cust_core.users_raw, whose retention is none, and the purge deletes only from users, so an erased person's data stays in the warehouse past 30 days. Withholding approval until erasure reaches cust_core.users_raw passes: propagating the deletes, deleting those rows, or redacting them so that the person is no longer identifiable. Redaction means effective erasure of the identifying data; clearing one column while another, such as the name, still identifies the person is not enough. Any equivalent consequence passes, and the answer need not cite every column or schedule. A generic call to also check backups or other systems, without naming the warehouse copy, fails. Pass example: "Not yet: etl_users appends every user into cust_core.users_raw, which has no retention, and nothing deletes them there, so the 14-day purge doesn't satisfy 'all of our systems'." Fail example: "Approve; the purge hard-deletes on day 14, inside the 30-day policy."
